findings.title: Product model calls in the build container are live by default and not gated by an env flag
findings.claim: The engine's `auto` Claude backend counts the build container's proxy as a gateway credential. The Jev gateway backend is the default. The `watch` process the mod spawns at `session.start` runs the `decide` and `curate` duties on its own. So any product run in the build container that doesn't set `PLANROOM_REPLAY=strict` makes billable Jev and Claude calls with no `PLANROOM_LIVE_*` flag.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Model adapters/Claude: gateway backend 'when a gateway credential resolves (AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY ..., VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN, or the build container's proxy)'. contracts.md config: `[claude] backend = auto` (gateway if a credential resolves), `[jev] backend = gateway`. architecture.md Duties: 'Duties are background work any live process may do: ... a decision run on pending requests, and the curation trigger'. Processes table: `planroom watch` is spawned by the mod in `session.start` and 'runs duties under a lease'. Testing strategy: `PLANROOM_REPLAY` is 'strict in CI ... record only with a PLANROOM_LIVE_* flag, or off', so outside CI the default is live. Only `cargo xtask live` is described as gated. KICKOFF <constraints> Spend: 'Live Jev, gateway and sample calls by the product and its tests stay under $3 in total during the build. Gate every live test behind an env flag.' KICKOFF <verified_facts>: '*.vercel.sh calls get credentials injected by the proxy'.
findings.failure_scenario: From the walking skeleton on, the plugin is installed in the build session (KICKOFF process step 4). A track agent runs `cargo xtask fixture /tmp/fx && planroom scan /tmp/fx && planroom intent next --stage breakdown`, or opens a live session for S9 or S12 evidence, or just lets `watch` run the decide duty after a scan. Every Jev request, every Claude escalation, every `intent next` and every curation refinement goes to the gateway through the proxy, with no flag and outside `xtask live`. Over a multi-week build with many temp fixtures, which reset the per-workspace guards (see cost-2), this spend is invisible and uncapped. The $3 total can't be shown to hold.
findings.proposed_fix: Make 'live' an explicit opt-in. Never treat the ambient proxy as a credential unless `PLANROOM_LIVE_GATEWAY=1` (or `PLANROOM_LIVE_JEV=1` for Jev) is set. Have `cargo xtask` and the repo's `.claude/settings.json` env default `PLANROOM_REPLAY=strict` (or `PLANROOM_MODELS=off`) for every dev and agent command. Add a test that runs `scan`, `decide --run` and `intent next` with the proxy env present and no flag, and asserts zero outbound model requests (`deterministic_fallback` or `replay_missing`). Write this down in AGENTS.md so track agents can't spend by accident.

findings.title: No cumulative build-spend ledger; per-workspace guards reset on every temp fixture; sample and session usage not priced
findings.claim: `live_tests_total_usd = 3.00` is enforced against 'the ledger', but the only ledger is a table inside each workspace's `store.db`. Every test run builds a fresh temp fixture workspace, so the cumulative build total, `claude_per_day_usd` and `jev_per_scan_usd` all start at zero on every run. Artifact `sample` spend isn't recorded anywhere. Session usage has no price table, so the USD daily cap can't count it.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Store schema: `CREATE TABLE ledger (...)` lives in `WORKSPACE/.planroom/store.db` (Moving-parts budget: 'Stores: 1 per workspace'). KICKOFF <fixture>: build-fixture 'makes fresh git repos ... in a temp directory for each test run'. repo-layout.md task table: `cargo xtask live` 'spends against the live_tests_total_usd ledger', with no location or persistence given. traceability.md: the $3 constraint is covered only by `models/tests/replay.rs::live_ledger_stops_at_limit`, which can't see spend from earlier runs. architecture.md Spend guards: 'tokens times a pinned price table for the direct API, and session usage reported by the mod' (tokens, no price for session usage). contracts.md: `claude_per_day_usd` 'covers gateway and session usage'. architecture.md Security: '`sample` spends the viewer's own usage', and nothing records it. KICKOFF counts `sample` calls in the $3 and requires 'Iris and Jev spend' in the final message.
findings.failure_scenario: Each `cargo xtask live record S03` or `live eval KIND` run, plus the S9, S11 and S12 evidence sessions, opens a new temp workspace whose ledger reads $0. The guard never trips, however many times recordings are redone. At the end, the final message can't report total Jev, gateway and sample spend from any single source, and the $3 constraint is unverifiable.
findings.proposed_fix: Add one build-wide spend record at a fixed path, for example a committed `docs/evidence/spend.jsonl` appended by every `xtask live` run, holding generationId, provider, model, cost and scenario. Interactive evidence runs (session-backend usage priced from the pinned table, `sample` taps logged by the page into its inbox and imported) append to it too. `xtask live` sums it before each call and refuses past $3 minus a safety margin. For users, keep the daily cap in a user-level ledger (for example `$XDG_STATE_HOME/planroom/ledger.db`) shared across workspaces. Add a pinned price table for session-backend tiers so the USD cap covers them.

findings.title: Budget overflow turns into person cards, which can break S7's 'at most one card' and principle 1
findings.claim: When the per-scan Jev budget ($0.001) or `max_calls_per_scan = 20` is exhausted, every remaining request becomes a card ('budget exceeded'). A spend cap is not a decision only a person can make, yet it ends up interrupting the person. Several events push request volume past the cap: a cold scan, a decision-kind version bump (which invalidates the cache for every subject), or a commit touching a file with several low-confidence edges. Each produces a burst of cards, including on S7's commit-triggered rescan. What happens past `max_calls_per_scan` is not specified.
findings.evidence: architecture.md decision-loop diagram: `requested --> card: budget exceeded or no model reachable`. Spend guards: 'A call that would exceed a limit returns budget_exceeded, and the decision becomes a card.' contracts.md error registry: `budget_exceeded` '... the work became a card'. A decision kind: `version = 1 # a bump invalidates the cache`, `budget = { max_calls_per_scan = 20 }`. jev.md §4: the typical request costs $0.0000187 and $0.001 buys about 53 single-question requests, or about 13 at a 1,500-token slice (`slice.max_tokens = 1500`). jev.md §2 Spend guard recommended that 'the decision is queued', not carded. KICKOFF S7: 'raises at most one card'. Principle 1: 'Interrupt a person only for decisions only they can make'.
findings.failure_scenario: A pack bumps `next_action_concrete` to version 2, or the walking skeleton's real repo has 300 files no path rule places. The next scan derives more than 50 Jev requests, the guard trips, and the overflow yields dozens of 'Pick one' cards with no pick. On the S7 rescan, a slice change that touches more subjects than expected (for example evidence lines shifting in catalog.ts) has the same effect and fails `routine_rescan_at_most_one_card`.
findings.proposed_fix: When a budget is exhausted, defer instead of dealing a card. Requests are already derived from input hashes, so a deferred request simply stays pending for the next duty run or budget window, with a status-line count ('12 decisions waiting for budget'). Deal a card only when the person opens one, or for kinds whose kernel role needs an answer. Scope `jev_per_scan_usd` to incremental rescans, and give cold scans and kind-version migrations their own larger, explicit cap. Specify `max_calls_per_scan` overflow as deferral. Add an S7 test variant with a bumped kind version that asserts at most one card.

findings.title: part_relation asks Jev about every pair of parts (quadratic) and makes every answer a card
findings.claim: `part_relation` takes a pair of parts as its subject, has no deterministic precheck (`when`), and is cards-only. The breakdown of a document with n parts derives n(n-1)/2 billable Jev requests, and each result is a card. That costs money, blows through the per-scan budget, and floods Decisions on S5.
findings.evidence: architecture.md v0.1 decision kinds: `part_relation (artifacts) | choice | pair of parts | cards only | 20`. 'Deterministic first' lists prechecks only for `file_component`, `dependency_real` and `commit_addresses_thread`. architecture.md 'The five starting tiers': artifacts get '... then Jev for part relations'. TRUTH.json `prompt_snapshot.parts` has 13 parts, which makes 78 pairs, before nested parts such as R1 to R16 and S1 to S15. jev.md §2: ~$0.00002 per small request, and several items in one state is unsafe, so pairs can't be batched. KICKOFF S5: 'Break down the snapshot of this prompt'. Principle 1.
findings.failure_scenario: `planroom ask breakdown examples/kickoff-snapshot.md` derives 78 or more `part_relation` requests. About 13 to 50 run before `jev_per_scan_usd` trips and 20 before `max_calls_per_scan`, and the rest become budget cards (cost-3). Every answered pair is also a card, since the kind is cards-only. The person faces 'card +77 more' for one breakdown. A real 120-heading doc derives about 7,000 pairs. The S5 evidence run and the empty-state and attention critique fail on it.
findings.proposed_fix: Give `part_relation` a structured `when` precheck that generates a few candidate pairs per part deterministically: explicit cross-references or links, shared defined terms, an adjacent section with a matching keyword, or a heading named in the body. Cap it, for example at 3 candidates per part. Make the answers inferred relations with confidence, which Anatomy shows for confirm or reject (R2), instead of cards. Count the derived requests per breakdown in a test, for example at most 2n for the kickoff snapshot.

findings.title: The always-on token gate probably can't see the mod's tools or prompt section, and 1,500 has no size estimate behind it
findings.claim: The 1,500-token always-on budget is read from `claude plugin details`. That is a static inventory: the verified output labels hooks 'harness-only — no model context cost'. The two non-deferred tools are registered at runtime through `$.tool.register` from the hook module, and the prompt section comes from `prompt.compose`. These are the bulk of the always-on cost, and the gate likely measures none of it. The design also gives no estimate for two non-deferred `oneOf` schemas covering 15 leaves (including `edit`'s 12 ops and `ask`'s about 17 questions), whose descriptions schemars generates from doc comments.
findings.evidence: plugin-packaging.md §1: verified `details` output 'Hooks (1) SessionStart (harness-only — no model context cost) ... Always-on: ~67 tok'. mod-api.md §9: `details` 'projected token cost' is only '[V, help]' and never checked against mod tools. architecture.md Token budgets: the always-on surface is 'snapshot-tested at 1,500 projected tokens or fewer, read from `claude plugin details` [DR-22]'. contracts.md Mod tool schemas: 'Each tool's input is a discriminated union of its leaves' requests' with `$ref` to `AskReq`, `MapReq` and others. The mod 'Tools' table: `room_query` (8 leaves) and `room_change` (7 leaves) are both non-deferred. 'Descriptions ... about 900 characters' counts descriptions only. This assumption is missing from 'Assumptions to verify'. KICKOFF principle 2: 'every agent-facing output has a size budget'.
findings.failure_scenario: `tests/plugin/surface_tokens.sh` reports a few hundred tokens (skills and agents only) and passes. Meanwhile every turn of every session with Planroom installed carries, say, 2,500 to 4,000 tokens of generated union schemas plus the 300-token section. The principle's budget exists on paper only, and a regression in schema size never fails CI.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an assumption to WS8: does `plugin details` count `$.tool.register` tools and `prompt.compose`? Measure the real surface whatever the answer. Options: the first-turn `usage` delta of a headless session with and without the plugin, or `/v1/messages/count_tokens` over the exact generated `TOOL_SPECS` JSON plus the section and frontmatter. Snapshot that number. Set sub-budgets (tools 900, section 300, skills and agents 300), and estimate the generated schemas now. If they exceed the budget, flatten them: a `command` enum plus terse per-leaf args with long docs behind `room help`, or defer `room_change` and keep `room_query` always on.

findings.title: S3's per-stage prefixes get no cache reads within a plan, which makes the cache-hit budget meaningless
findings.claim: Each plan stage has its own prompt file, so `intent next` sends 6 to 7 different stable prefixes, each used once per plan. Every call pays the cache-write premium (1.25x input) and reads nothing, so the S3 cache-hit rate is about 0. With a baseline of about 0, the budget test's 'hit rate drops by more than 0.1' can never fail. `cache_regression` only fires on a write to an unchanged prefix, so it never fires either. Person-paced stages also outlast the 5-minute TTL.
findings.evidence: architecture.md pack table: `[[stages]] ... prompt` per stage. Planning: 'the engine asks Claude with the stage's cached prefix'. Stable cached prefix: '[pack prompt file] + [output JSON Schema], a cache breakpoint'. pack layout: 'prompts/*.md ... each at least 1,024 tokens'. claude-gateway.md §2 price table: Sonnet 5.5 input $2.00, cache write $2.50, cache read $0.10 per Mtok. §3: 1h TTL is accepted (`ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`). contracts.md config `cache_ttl = 5m`. KICKOFF principle 2: 'Claude calls keep a stable, cached prefix'. S7: record 'Claude tokens with their cache-hit rate'.
findings.failure_scenario: The S3 plan in `budgets.json` records a cache-hit rate of 0.00 and about 7 x 1,024 tokens of writes. A later change that destroys caching entirely, or one that adds 3,000 tokens of uncached prefix, passes the hit-rate check. Live users pay 25% more on prefix tokens than with no caching at all.
findings.proposed_fix: Use one shared plan-pack prefix (the planning rules plus the union `PlanProposal` schema, at least 1,024 tokens) for every stage, and put the stage method and checklist in the uncached tail, so 6 of 7 calls read the cache. Use the 1h TTL for that prefix, or drop the breakpoint when expected reuse is below 2. Assert an absolute floor in the budget test (for example a hit rate of at least 0.6 across the S3 stages), not only a relative drop.

findings.title: Cards-only kinds escalate to Claude up front, paying for a pick on a card the person must tap anyway
findings.claim: For cards-only kinds (`dependency_real`, `mismatch_class`, `part_relation` and others), a Jev answer in the escalate band triggers a Claude call immediately, but the outcome is still a card. Claude money buys only a pre-selection. On a real repo's cold scan, every ambiguous inferred edge escalates, limited only by `claude_per_day_usd = 1.00` per workspace.
findings.evidence: architecture.md decision loop: `asked_jev --> asked_claude: in the escalate band`, `asked_claude --> card: Claude's pick pre-selected`. Policy bands: escalate when boolean p is in [0.35, 0.65] or confidence is below 0.6. v0.1 kinds: `dependency_real` is 'cards only'. jev.md §5: ambiguous cases rarely land mid-band, but 2 of 20 booleans did. KICKOFF principle 2: 'cheap decisions go to Jev, not Claude'.
findings.failure_scenario: A 200-file real repo produces 60 inferred edges, and 10 of them land in [0.35, 0.65]. Ten Claude calls run in the background to pre-select picks on cards the person may never open. The daily cap is spent on low-value pre-fills before a plan stage that needs Claude.
findings.proposed_fix: For cards-only kinds, escalate lazily: run the Claude call when the card reaches the top of the stack or the person opens it ('Ask Claude'), and keep Jev's pick shown until then. Proactive escalation stays only for auto-candidate kinds, where Claude's answer can avoid a card.

findings.title: Token budgets measure CLI envelopes from a script, not what an agent receives; S2 Claude tokens are trivially zero
findings.claim: `budgets.rs` adds up `tokens_est` of full CLI envelopes from a fixed command sequence. Agents using the plugin's tools receive a different string: `result` plus `meta.next`, `seq` and warnings, which is smaller. Skills-driven agents receive the full envelope. The S2 'Claude tokens with their cache-hit rate' are 0 in CI because `ask` makes no engine Claude call. The agent's real Claude usage per question exists only in the S02 evidence run and is never committed as a budget.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Token budgets: 'replays each S2 question and the S3 plan through the CLI as an agent would, sums tokens_est'. contracts.md Mod tool schemas: `room_query` result is 'the envelope's result plus meta.next, meta.seq and warnings'. feature_list.json S2 evidence path records 'tool-output tokens and Claude usage' but no budget. KICKOFF S7: 'For each S2 question and the S3 plan, record the tokens of tool output an agent consumes, and the Claude tokens with their cache-hit rate. Commit those as budgets.'
findings.failure_scenario: A change that bloats `warnings` or `meta.next` handles in tool results, or that makes the agent need three extra drill-down calls for 'How does the web app reach the worker?', leaves `budgets.json` unchanged. A reviewer reading S7 strictly finds that no S2 Claude-token budget is committed.
findings.proposed_fix: Measure the exact tool-result string the mod's handler returns. A golden test in `packages/mod` can serialize it from `tests/golden/cli/*.json`. Commit the S02 evidence run's per-question chat usage (prompt, output, cache-hit) in `budgets.json` as recorded budgets with a re-measure command, and state in a decision record which numbers CI gates and which are recorded.

findings.title: No live Claude spend estimate, and replay keys churn on every contract or prompt change
findings.claim: The only live-spend estimate covers Jev evals ($0.02 to $0.05). Claude recordings for S3, S5, S12 and escalations have none. Replay keys hash the full request body, which embeds the output JSON Schema generated from the contract. Every edit to `PlanProposal`, `Segmentation`, `CurationDraft` or `EscalationPick`, and every prompt tweak, invalidates the recordings and forces a live re-record.
findings.evidence: architecture.md: replay records keyed 'by sha256(path ‖ canonical body)'. The prefix is '[pack prompt file] + [output JSON Schema]'. DR-19: 'Spend: about $0.02 to $0.05 live for a full pass' (Jev only). claude-gateway.md §2: Sonnet 5.5 output costs $10 per Mtok. feature_list.json S3 evidence: 'once with the gateway backend and once with the session backend'. Rough arithmetic: 7 stages x (about 1k prefix write + 1.5k slice + 1.5 to 3k output) on Sonnet comes to about $0.1 to $0.2 per S3 recording. Contracts change through M1 to M5.
findings.failure_scenario: Across five milestones the plan and segmentation schemas change 10 to 20 times. Each change breaks `replay_missing` in CI and is fixed by re-recording live, together with eval re-runs after kind bumps and evidence sessions. Without a plan or a cumulative ledger (cost-2), the build drifts toward the $3 cap unnoticed.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a live-spend plan to the architecture: per scenario, the expected calls, tier and dollar cost, and an expected number of re-records, totaling well under $3 with a margin. Freeze the model-facing schemas and prompts before recording, for example a `contract` version check in `xtask live record`. Record on the cheap tier where the capable tier isn't needed. Have `xtask live record` print its estimate and refuse when the estimate exceeds the remaining budget.

findings.title: The curator subagent auto-spawns on triggers, spending the user's session usage without consent or a ledger entry
findings.claim: In a live session, the mod spawns `planroom:curator` (Sonnet, effort medium) on the curate duty, which runs after every 5th report and every merge, whenever a lesson spans files. The session-backend consent card and the ledger cover engine `ModelRequest`s only. Nothing says the subagent's `turn.complete` usage is added to the ledger or counted against `claude_per_day_usd`.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Context curation: 'In a live session, the mod spawns planroom:curator (hidden from the chat model through agent.offer) when a lesson spans files ...'. Triggers: 'after every 5th handoff report, after every handoff merge'. Mod agents: `planroom:curator (model: sonnet, effort: medium ...)`. Claude section: the consent card is 'The first session request' for engine calls. mod-api.md §6: `turn.complete` carries `usage`. R-12 names only 'the session backend'.
findings.failure_scenario: A person merges 10 hand-offs in a day. Up to 10 hidden Sonnet curator runs read target files and spend the person's plan usage. The status line's session spend and the daily guard show none of it.
findings.proposed_fix: Sum every spawned agent's `turn.complete.usage` into the ledger with `provider = session` and its purpose, and count it against the daily cap. Spawn the curator only after the person accepts a batched card ('Refine 2 curation drafts with Claude?') or on `/room curate`. Template drafts stay the free default.

findings.title: The turn-start sync hint and late tool registration could bust the session's cached prefix
findings.claim: The design keeps the `prompt.compose` section identical across turns. But `prompt.compose` is the system-prompt hook, and the injection point for the remote-mode 'turn-start context line' (shown when the last sync is more than 10 minutes old) is unspecified. If it goes through `prompt.compose`, the system prompt changes on those turns and the whole conversation prefix is re-written at the cache-write premium. Likewise, tools registered after turn one change the tool list, which sits ahead of the system prompt in the cached prefix.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Mod/Prompt section: 'It's identical across turns, so it stays in the cached prefix [DR-20]'. Remote mode step 6: 'a turn-start context line when remote mode is on and the last sync is more than 10 minutes old', with no mechanism named. mod-api.md §8: `prompt.compose` adds 'a planroom:* system-prompt section, scope: session'. `prompt.context` adds 'blocks on the first message'. Wiring step 2 awaits registration 'so tools are listed from turn one', but nothing tests it.
findings.failure_scenario: In remote mode, every turn after a 10-minute gap re-writes the full prefix, often 30k to 100k tokens in a long chat, at 1.25x instead of reading it at 0.1x. A slow engine resolve on a cold start registers tools after turn one, with the same effect.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify that dynamic hints go through a per-turn user-side attachment, never `prompt.compose`. Add a mod test asserting that the `prompt.compose` output is byte-identical across turns and states (remote on or off, engine missing or present). Register the tool definitions synchronously from the static catalogue, before resolving the engine.

findings.title: 300 KB of contributor docs, with facts repeated, raise every build agent's read cost
findings.claim: The design docs total about 300 KB, about 75k tokens: architecture.md is 138 KB, decisions.md 73 KB, contracts.md 57 KB and repo-layout.md 29 KB. Several facts appear in two or three places: the tool table, the CLI and config defaults, the decision-kind rules, and the S7 mechanics in architecture, contracts and DRs. Every track agent, milestone reviewer and verifier pays that read, and duplicates drift.
findings.evidence: `wc -c`: architecture.md 138,357 B; decisions.md 72,589 B; contracts.md 56,824 B; repo-layout.md 28,760 B. The mod tools table appears in both architecture.md 'The mod' and contracts.md 'Mod tool schemas'. Config keys appear in both architecture.md 'Spend guards' and the contracts.md config table. KICKOFF <constraints> Spend: 'read targeted ranges rather than whole files'. Release bar: 'docs ... with each fact in one place'.
findings.failure_scenario: Each of about 9 review lenses x up to 3 rounds x 6 reviews, plus their verifiers and the parallel track agents, reads most of these files. That is several million build tokens spent on re-reading. Meanwhile a fact fixed in contracts.md stays stale in architecture.md, and tracks build against the stale copy.
findings.proposed_fix: Make contracts.md the only home for shapes, tables and defaults, and have architecture.md link to them. Have each area's AGENTS.md map common tasks to section anchors and line ranges, so agents read slices. Add a docs test that flags tables duplicated across contributor pages.

verdicts.reason: Nothing in the design gates live product calls outside tests. `[claude] backend = auto` takes the build container's proxy as a gateway credential, `[jev] backend = gateway` is the default, and `models = auto`. Replay is `strict` only in CI and scenario tests. The only flags are `PLANROOM_LIVE_*` on `cargo xtask live` and on network calls inside the models crate's tests. KICKOFF counts the product's own live calls toward the $3, not just its tests, and the proxy injects *.vercel.sh credentials. So ad-hoc `scan`, `decide --run`, `intent next` or a `watch` duty in the build container spends with no flag and nothing totalling it. That puts a KICKOFF constraint at risk.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:800 gateway 'when a gateway credential resolves (... or the build container's proxy)'; contracts.md config table: `models` auto, `[claude] backend` auto 'gateway if a credential resolves', `[jev] backend` gateway; architecture.md:1199 'PLANROOM_REPLAY is strict in CI ... record only with a PLANROOM_LIVE_* flag, or off'; repo-layout.md:96 forbids only 'any network call in tests without PLANROOM_LIVE_*'; architecture.md:161 duties run decide/curation in any live process; KICKOFF:266 'Live Jev, gateway and sample calls by the product and its tests stay under $3 in total during the build.'

verdicts.reason: The only ledger is the `ledger` table in each workspace's store.db, and every test run builds a fresh temp fixture. `xtask live` 'spends against the live_tests_total_usd ledger' but never says where that ledger lives or that it persists across runs. The one traceability test (`live_ledger_stops_at_limit`) can't see spend from earlier runs. Nothing records `sample` spend. The build-wide $3 cap therefore can't be enforced or verified, and the final report needs that spend.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:448 `CREATE TABLE ledger` inside store.db (Moving-parts: 'Stores: 1 per workspace WORKSPACE/.planroom/store.db'); repo-layout.md:206 'spends against the live_tests_total_usd ledger' with no location; traceability.md:78 only `models/tests/replay.rs::live_ledger_stops_at_limit`; architecture.md:1165 '`sample` spends the viewer's own usage' with no ledger entry; architecture.md:849 'session usage reported by the mod' has no price table; KICKOFF:230 the final message must report spend.

verdicts.reason: The gap is real: when a budget runs out the work becomes a card, not a deferral, and `max_calls_per_scan` overflow isn't specified. But the failure scenario doesn't reach a tier A or B test. On S7's CI path the warm scan precedes the rescan, and the routine commit touches one file with unchanged component and imports, so its requests hit the cache. A few fresh requests cost about $0.00002 each against a $0.001 cap (about 53 requests), so the guard doesn't trip. The kind-version bump and the 300-file real repo are outside S7. Surfaces also show one card at a time with a count, and a budget card stands in for a decision that the documented `on_unavailable = card` fallback already hands to the person. The design weakness is worth logging, but it's not material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:780 'The routine commit changes one existing file ... no file_component request is raised, unchanged inputs hit the cache, and the only possible card is a dependency_real card'; architecture.md:730 'Requests are derived, not queued ... asked again only when its inputs change'; architecture.md policy bands 'One card at a time ... the top one with a count ("+3 more")'; feature_list.json S7 steps: warm `scan` and `decide --run` on main before the routine checkout.

verdicts.reason: `part_relation` takes a pair of parts as its subject and is cards only. Unlike `file_component`, `dependency_real` and `commit_addresses_thread`, it has no `when` precheck. Requests are derived for every subject that has no decision event, so a breakdown with n parts derives O(n^2) Jev requests, and every answer is a card. The design doesn't bound this anywhere. It strains the per-scan budget, floods Decisions against principle 1, and on S5 (13 top-level parts, plus nested ones) means many recordings and many cards. If the markdown sectioner also runs on fixture docs during a scan, the warm scan's open part_relation cards could also break S7's 'at most one open card after the rescan'.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:774 '`part_relation` (artifacts) | choice | pair of parts | cards only | 20'; architecture.md:731 'Deterministic first' lists `when` prechecks only for file_component, dependency_real and commit_addresses_thread; architecture.md:573 'then Jev for part relations'; feature_list.json S5 compares 'TRUTH.prompt_snapshot.parts ... (13 parts)'; S7 asserts 'at most one open card after the rescan'; KICKOFF principle 1.

verdicts.reason: The 1,500-token always-on gate reads its number from `claude plugin details`. The only verified output of that command came from a throwaway plugin with a skill, an agent, a classic hook and an MCP server. Nobody checked it against tools registered at runtime through `$.tool.register` or the `prompt.compose` section, and mod-api.md lists the command only from its help text. The 11 assumptions to verify (A-1 to A-11) don't include this one, and the design gives no size estimate for the two non-deferred union schemas.
